reading: The same new cable put into walls of two kinds of house. Most new US homes, timber frame: pulled through holes drilled in the studs, behind the board; quick. Most German homes, one plastered brick wall done two ways. Repainted: a duct screwed onto the surface and painted over; quick, but the old wall is unchanged and the duct stays on show. Renovated: a channel cut, the cable laid and plastered over; slow, and the channel stays as a scar.
sourceNote: No numbers are drawn; no hours or days are given. The labels describe general building practice for timber stud walls and plastered solid brick walls; the analogy is the owner's (transcript 2026-11-16-020) and the plan's analogy dictionary (plan-restart.md, rows 'Timber frame', 'Brick', 'Fresh paint on the facade': paint is a new part put on the old wall while the wall stays as it was). 'Most new US homes' / 'most German homes' are the owner's framing of the analogy, to be backed by the construction sources the plan names for section 0.
